preamble: Diphthongization of a long mid back vowel [oː] into the wide falling diphthong [aʊ̯]: the nucleus lowers and unrounds, and the rounded high offglide stays. In Swabian (Alemannic), Middle High German long ô merged with â and ou into [aʊ̯], giving hoch [hoːx] > hau 'high'. The change is rare. Most o-diphthongizations stop at [ou] or [ɔu] (see o_to_ou).

examples.from: Middle High German hôch 'high' (Standard German hoch [hoːx])
examples.note: Middle High German long ô is regularly [aʊ̯] in Swabian, merging with the reflexes of â and ou.

examples.from: Middle High German schône 'already' (Standard German schon [ʃoːn])
examples.note: The same development, with loss of the final nasal.

sources: Russ, C. V. J. (1990). Swabian. In C. V. J. Russ (Ed.), The Dialects of Modern German: A Linguistic Survey (pp. 337–363). Routledge.
